newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-FRANCE WITHOUT PIERCE AGAINST BELGIUM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FRANCE WITHOUT PIERCE AGAINST BELGIUM.

text.p: France will do without two leading players in the singles of their Fed Cup semifinal against Belgium over the weekend.
Team captain Yannick Noah confirmed on Friday that French number one Mary Pierce had not sufficiently recovered from an arm injury to play.
But the former French Open winner, who also skippers France's Davis Cup team, made a far more surprising decision by dropping Wimbledon quarter-finalist Nathalie Tauziat from both singles.
Tauziat, ranked 21st in the world, will only take part in the doubles.
Instead, Noah picked hopefuls Sandrine Testud and Alexandra Fusai for the singles, which will be played on clay.
Testud, 20th in the WTA rankings, caused a sensation at Wimbledon by beating former world number one Monica Seles. Fusai is a modest 57th in the world but is arguably better on clay than Tauziat.
Belgium announced a far less surprising squad with Sabine Appelmans and Dominique van Roost their singles players, Els Callens and Laurence Courtois their doubles pair.
Noah gave his team an even chance of beating the Belgians, who sprung a surprise with their 5-0 rout of Spain in the first round in March.
"Between the two teams I think it's 50-50. And that's not just a way of handling the pressure to say that. I really think it will be a balanced match," he said.
